compiled_state.title: As an epic stakeholder, I want a 5-site measurement harness proving >=70% return-block token reduction post-migration, so that the epic's context-cost claim is empirically verified
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Build a measurement harness that captures pre- and post-migration return-block sizes (in tokens) for each of the 5 cited sites, computes per-site and aggregate percent reduction, and gates a pass at >=70% aggregate. Pin tokenizer, fixed test epic, and HEAD-vs-HEAD comparison protocol so the measurement is reproducible.

**Why**: sc-7 is the only SC tied to the epic's value claim; staging it as its own story lets it run after the migration lands without blocking earlier stories.

**Scope**:
- IN: harness records baseline return-block token counts for the 5 sites (using pre-migration snapshots or replay on the pre-migration HEAD commit), records post-migration counts on post-migration HEAD, computes per-site and aggregate reduction, and gates a pass at >=70% aggregate. Output is a machine-readable JSON report committed to or attached to the epic for audit. Tokenizer is named and pinned; a fixed test epic id is named in the harness config.
- OUT: changing the migration itself (separate story), tuning the CLI (separate story).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, the harness captures pre-migration return-block token counts for all 5 cited sites (impl-plan :511, :978, :1238; preplanning :513; sprint :2332) on a checkout of pre-migration HEAD (commit SHA recorded in the report)
  ← Satisfies: sc-7
- When this story is complete, the harness captures post-migration return-block token counts for the same 5 sites on post-migration HEAD (commit SHA recorded in the report) and computes per-site and aggregate percent reduction
  ← Satisfies: sc-7
- When this story is complete, the tokenizer used for measurement is named and pinned (e.g., the Anthropic claude tokenizer via the official endpoint, or a documented char-to-token proxy with stated approximation), and the same tokenizer is used for both pre- and post-migration counts
  ← Satisfies: sc-7
- When this story is complete, a fixed test epic id is named in the harness config and used identically for pre- and post-migration runs; the harness fails if the named epic is missing
  ← Satisfies: sc-7
- When this story is complete, aggregate token reduction across the 5 sites is >=70%, and the harness emits a machine-readable JSON report recording per-site numbers, aggregate percent, both HEAD SHAs, and the tokenizer name
  ← Satisfies: sc-7
- When this story is complete, the report is committed to the epic (as a scratch artifact, attachment, or referenced file) so the audit trail records the measurement evidence
  ← Satisfies: sc-7
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
  ← Satisfies: sc-7

## Considerations

- [Methodology] Token-count methodology must be specified (which tokenizer, what counts as the return block) so pre/post are commensurate.
- [Stability] If post-migration return blocks vary by run, take the median across N runs rather than a single sample.
- [Acceptance-risk] If aggregate reduction is between 50–70%, the harness should surface a clear partial-pass signal rather than silently failing — the user may want to accept with rationale.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
